svg.title: The go-to sweep
svg.desc: The go-to sweep. One ship alone, ordered to fly to a circle. The same start is flown again and again, each time with a different time allowed. One start, two ways to fly it shows a map from above, with an azure fighter at lower left and a dashed azure target circle at lower right, labelled circle. An ember fighter sits just inside the curved map edge at the top, labelled parked enemy: it cannot shoot. A solid azure order line goes straight to the circle, labelled the script: straight there. A dashed azure route curves up, loops around the enemy below the map edge, then comes down to the circle, labelled many trained pilots: to the enemy first, then late. At an allowance of 2, trained pilots missed the most deadlines against the harmless parked enemy. What varies between starts has three mini maps, each with a lone azure ship, a route and a dashed target circle. Parked shows one enemy fighter at rest on the map's edge, which cannot shoot. One armed shows a script-flown fighter beside the route. Three armed shows a script-flown fighter, strafer and gunship beside the route. The lone ship is a fighter, strafer or gunship, 150, 300 or 500 m from the circle's edge. The circle's radius is 20 or 60 m. Six starts of each: 324 starts. The time allowed has a clock and a scale marked 0.8, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 5 and 8, with no deadline set apart at the right. A bracket under 0.8 and 1 says at or past what a ship can do. An allowance of 2 is twice the time a straight flight at full speed takes, plus 3 s to turn. Each start is flown at every allowance, and once with no deadline. Then it counts as in time if it arrives within twice the straight flight plus 10 s. The match clock is the same at every allowance, so it gives nothing away. A pilot that reads the deadline flies differently at 2 than at 8. One that ignores it flies the same every time.
